message: In the twin under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, mass on spring with damper tuned to bridge mode) retrofit concept, the tuning basis has 1.81 hertz versus 1.86 hertz question raised by Manager, thank you Manager. To check it I used vetted Den Hartog calculation (the Den Hartog optimum result (E3)). I found 1.81 hertz at 5.0 percent mass ratio from 500 kilograms over 10000 kilograms, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose retaining 1.81 hertz as correct optimum for chosen mass and noting 1.86 hertz corresponds to 2.0 percent ratio. My position: ready because mass-ratio dependence reconciles the difference. In the 40 metre footbridge baseline concept, the modal confirmation method has low damping baseline uncertainty. To check it I used mode layout with mass estimate (the under-deck layout sketch (E4) with the 10000 kilogram modal mass estimate (E2)). I found 1.9 hertz half-sine first vertical bending mode with antinode at midspan and about 0.4 percent inherent damping, according to Bachmann and Ammann, 1987. I propose twin 250 kilogram units at midspan below girders, thank you Retrofit Integration Architect and thank you Vibration Control Specialist. My position: ready because placement and frequency baseline are confirmed. In the same retrofit concept, the comfort verification method has acceleration acceptance question. To check it I used response simulation (the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6)). I found 0.74 metres per second squared with 9.44 percent effective damping versus 17.50 metres per second squared uncontrolled, according to Setra, 2006.
